metaDescription: Where to see the greater one-horned rhino in India: Kaziranga, Pobitora, Orang and Manas in Assam, and Jaldapara and Gorumara in West Bengal, with seasons.
description: A guide to seeing the greater one-horned rhinoceros in India: Kaziranga, which holds most of them, Pobitora near Guwahati, Orang and Manas in Assam, Jaldapara and Gorumara in the Dooars of West Bengal, and Dudhwa in Uttar Pradesh, with population figures, seasons, safari types and conservation history.
dek: India is home to most of the world's greater one-horned rhinos, almost all of them in Assam and northern West Bengal. Here is where to see them.

intro: The greater one-horned rhinoceros once ranged across the floodplains of northern India. Hunting and habitat loss reduced it to a few pockets, and by the early 20th century only a few dozen may have survived in Kaziranga. Protection has since brought numbers back to several thousand across India and Nepal.

In India, rhinos live mainly in Assam and in the Dooars of West Bengal, with a reintroduced population in Dudhwa, Uttar Pradesh. Rhinos graze in open grassland, so they are among the easier large animals to see.
quickAnswer: Kaziranga National Park in Assam has the largest population of greater one-horned rhinos in the world, 2,613 in the 2022 count. Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary near Guwahati has a very high density, and Orang and Manas have smaller populations. In West Bengal, Jaldapara and Gorumara national parks have rhinos. The season is roughly November to April.
takeaways: Kaziranga holds most of the world's greater one-horned rhinos.
Pobitora has one of the highest rhino densities anywhere, about an hour or so from Guwahati.
Jaldapara in West Bengal has India's second-largest rhino population.
Rhino parks are usually open from November to April and close in the monsoon.
Rhinos graze in open grassland, so sightings are more likely than for big cats.

items.name: Ranges and safaris
body: Kaziranga is divided into the Kohora (central), Bagori (western), Agaratoli (eastern) and Burapahar ranges. Jeep safaris run in all of them; elephant rides start from Kohora and Bagori early in the morning. The western range around Bagori is known for rhinos in open grassland.

image.alt: Visitors on elephants watching a one-horned rhino in the grassland of Kaziranga
image.caption: Rhino viewing in Kaziranga

items.name: Pobitora
body: A small sanctuary with a very dense rhino population, often seen on a day trip from Guwahati.

items.name: Orang
body: A national park on the north bank of the Brahmaputra, sometimes called a mini Kaziranga, with far fewer visitors.

items.name: Manas
body: Rhinos were lost here during years of unrest. They have been brought back since 2006, first as hand-raised calves and then by translocation under Indian Rhino Vision 2020.

sections.heading: The Dooars, West Bengal
paras: Jaldapara National Park, near Alipurduar, has India's second-largest rhino population. Gorumara, a smaller park nearby, has rhinos, gaur and elephants, seen from watchtowers and jeeps. Both close in the monsoon, roughly mid-June to mid-September.

image.alt: A one-horned rhinoceros grazing in tall grass in Jaldapara National Park
image.caption: A rhino in Jaldapara

sections.heading: Rhino conservation
paras: Poaching for horn remains the main threat. Assam's forest department, with guards and community support, has cut poaching sharply in recent years. Floods on the Brahmaputra also affect Kaziranga each monsoon, when animals move to highlands and across the national highway; speed limits are enforced on the road.

sections.heading: Tips for seeing rhinos
list: Morning safaris often find rhinos grazing in open grass or wallowing in pools.
Early in the season (November) grass can be tall; visibility improves after the grass is burned in winter.
Take drives in more than one range; each has a different mix of grassland, wetland and forest.
Combine Kaziranga with a visit to Guwahati for Kamakhya temple and the Brahmaputra.

safety: Rhinos can charge; stay in the vehicle and keep a distance.
Sightings are never guaranteed; wild animals move freely and every drive is different.
Wear a hat and sunscreen; grasslands give little shade.
Follow elephant-safari rules if you take one.
packing: Light layers and a warm jacket for winter mornings
